in_arabic.name: سليم
in_arabic.long_meaning: من أصوله العربية: سليم = سليمة (saleema) = أحوال أمانة, أمنة الحياة = safe, secure, protected

in_urdu.name: سليم
in_urdu.long_meaning: من انگریزی مائوری: Saleem = صليب (saleeb) = آمن, ممتنع (mamtuun) = protected, secure

in_hindi.name: सलीम
in_hindi.meaning: सुखी (sukhi) = happy, content, सफेद (safed) = white, pure, रक्षा (raksha) = protection
in_hindi.long_meaning: संस्कृत स्वरूप: सलीम = सुखी (sukhi) = आत्मा को सुख पहुंचने वाला, सफेद (safed) = शुद्ध, पवित्र, सफेद (raksha) = रक्षा = आत्मा का साथ, सुरक्षा

in_pashto.name: سليم
in_pashto.long_meaning: من أصوله الپشتو: سليم = سلامت (sulmat) = شانتاب (shantab) = سلامت, امانت, سختي (sakhti) = بیماری سے محفوظ رہنا, سلامت رہنا

in_english.name: Saleemuz
in_english.meaning: Saleem = safe, secure, protected, Saleemuz = belonging to Saleem
in_english.long_meaning:
From Arabic: Saleem = safe, secure, protected
From Persian suffix: -uz = belonging to, owner of
Therefore, Saleemuz = belonging to Saleem

historical_references.reference: Saleem-ud-din Yakub Shah, the last independent ruler of the Deccan Sultanate of Bahmani, reigned from 1482 to 1518.
historical_references.context: He is also known as Saleem Shah II and Saleem-ud-din Yakut. He was a significant figure in the late medieval period of India and is remembered for his attempts to centralize the Bahmani sultanate.

historical_references.reference: Saleem-ul-Marwan, a prominent Umayyad ghulam (slave soldier) during the time of the Caliphate of Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah (996-1021 AD), rose to prominence after the death of Al-Hakim and eventually seized the caliphate in 1021 AD.
historical_references.context: He ruled as the fifth caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate and is remembered for his ability to rule effectively during a tumultuous time in Islamic history.
